title: The Box from the South
subtitle: Don't flaunt your importance; let it speak for itself.

items.text: The Box from the South
VIP Room, Midnight Club

items.speaker: Drelome
items.text: Fleming, where did you manage to find forty thousand francs overnight?

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: There are opportunities everywhere, sir. You've just got to keep an eye out for them.
Monsieur Drelome arrives to meet with Fleming early in the morning, still obviously hungover from last night's drunken revelry.

items.speaker: Drelome
items.text: So, you won't be selling "The Merciful Maria" after all?

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: It looks like I won't have to; I've got time to spare and money to burn.

items.speaker: Drelome
items.text: I've heard it all before. Just remember, my offer for that pistol stands.

items.speaker: Drelome
items.text: But its value here will only drop with time.
Fleming leans back, relaxed.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: All I need to do now is move my shipment. Then I'll really be set.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: I doubt it'll take long. They're going to be begging for these beauties.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Picture it—you storming into your enemy's Christmas dinner with this beast, spitting lead at seven hundred rounds a minute.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Ten seconds—no, five—and the whole family is in hell.
Drelome raises a brow.

items.speaker: Drelome
items.text: How cruel.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: I'm not interested in judgment from a half-drunk loan shark.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Now make yourself scarce. I've got more important guests coming.

items.speaker: Drelome
items.text: Whatever you say. But just remember, if things fall through, I'm always ready to make a deal.
The pawnbroker stumbles out, either unconcerned or too bleary-eyed to care.
Fleming pours himself another drink, tapping his foot, waiting for the woman who can bring him two diamonds.
Ten minutes later, the door opens and Adelita steps in lightly. Fleming rises to greet her.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: We meet again, Mr. Longen. I do hope it won't be a wasted trip.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: One way or another, we'll soon find out.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Where's Madame Cosette?

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: However in the world would I know? We never agreed on when to meet. I came now only because it was convenient.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: So, do we wait for her?

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: Brette isn't part of this game. As long as we can return her diamond, that's enough.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: ... True. No point wasting time.
He raps the safe's sturdy lock with his knuckle.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Then take out the "Box from the South" and place it on the table.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: If you're telling the truth, that should mean there are two diamonds inside.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: Let me think through that long code ...
She turns the lock with ease and opens the safe. The "Box from the South" lies inside, unchanged.
She lifts it out, sets it on the table, and with the same motion as last night, unlatches the lid ...
Two diamonds of equal size rest on the velvet cushion. That much is undeniable.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: As you can see, this is the diamond Brette provided—along with its copy.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: I trust you remember its value. Twenty thousand francs. By our agreement, you should return my collateral.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Th—this is impossible ...
Fleming no longer cares about the money. He crouches over, stroking the miraculous box.
Despite his disbelief, he finds an impulse surging up inside him.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: I want that box. Name your price.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: A gun.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: A gun?

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Heh, I've got plenty of guns. I'd sell you one for a hundred and fifty dollars ...

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: But I have my sights on a very particular one.
Fleming lets go of the box, his thin lips pressing into a hard line.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: "The Merciful Maria."

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: That's the one. A beautiful little pistol. It once belonged to a Mafia matriarch—and it was said that it could tell who was a traitor.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: Fire it at your own men, and if they're loyal, the bullets will spare every vital point of the targets.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: You've heard of it.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: Call it a hobby. I like digging into and collecting such curious things.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: And while I've heard less-than-pleasant rumors, I personally don't care how the gun ended up in your hands.
Hurried footsteps sound outside the door. Moments later, "Brette" flings herself into the room.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Perfect. I'm glad to see you're still here, Adelita.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: Brette?

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: You've come at just the right time, Madame. Come, take a look—

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: She's deceiving you, Mr. Longen. The "Box from the South" is nothing but a cheap trick.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: What are you saying? I saw it with my own eyes. Look at another stone, identical as far as I can tell. Though maybe you ought to take a look.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I have no doubt the diamond is real. But the "Box from the South" is far from the life's work of an arcanist.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: It's only a jeweled puzzle box.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: Brette, please, I really don't appreciate this attempt at ruining my deal.
Without another word, Tennant draws her pistol and fires, striking the box's lid dead on.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: —Good God!
The lid shatters into powder, spilling several diamonds across the table.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: These diamonds ... where did they come from?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: They were hidden in the lid. All you need to do is turn the spring, and one will pop out every eight hours.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: From your point of view, it would seem like it was creating diamonds from thin air.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: It's a clever trick, isn't it? With six stones in reserve, it would take another two days before you'd realize something had gone wrong.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Have I got that right, Adelita?
The startled woman steps back from the shattered remains of the box.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: I don't really know all the details; I didn't make it. It just happened to fall into my hands.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I hate to think you were fooled by this, Fleming. I should expect it's clear as day to you now.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: You investigated it?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: It was my diamond inside that box. It was entirely in my interest to know its secrets.
Fleming glares at Adelita.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: You were after my pistol from the very start!
Her scheme laid bare, Adelita offers no defense.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: I never meant for things to be like this ... I should go.
Fleming slams his palm on the remains of the box, sending small pieces flying off.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Go? You think I'm gonna just let you walk out of here?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Let her go, Fleming.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: What?!

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: She's a fraud; we can see that plain as day. But I do hope you can see why violence wouldn't be good for any of us.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: So what, she just gets away with making a fool of me? Like I'm just some dumbass tourist to be fleeced?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Fleeced? Take a look at what you have right in front of you.
He glances down at the table strewn with shards and at last grasps "Brette's" point.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Diamonds.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Just think of these diamonds as your "damages." Aside from my own, of course. The rest should come out to one hundred and twenty thousand francs.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: I think you'll find they're worth even more than that. I choose them specifically—

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Don't push your luck, Adelita. We're letting you walk away without harming a pretty hair on your head.
She hesitates, her eyes lingering on the diamonds with a defeated and wistful expression.
But she has to choose.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: ... I suppose I have no choice.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Get out. And don't ever let me see your face again, swindler!
Adelita whirls and makes for the door, brushing past Tennant on her way out.

items.speaker: Adelita
items.text: I won't forget this, Brette.
With the con artist gone, Fleming plucks the scattered diamonds up from the table, his lips twitching into a crooked grin.
—A bruised ego traded for a hundred and twenty thousand francs. Not a bad bargain.
He tosses a diamond to Tennant.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Sit with me, Brette. I owe a loyal friend my thanks.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Didn't you say you were curious about my "typewriters"?
